reviews.review_text:

Extraordinary cultural and traditional music experience!
May 2026 • Couples
A cultural experience like no other!

Well, we certainly weren’t expecting this when we were looking for a place to have our final dinner in Hue. However, it wasn’t a restaurant, it was someone’s home. Owners Ngo and Camille welcomed us by name. The evening began with Ngo taking us on a tour of the spectacular grounds. When we asked whether we should wait for the other guests before continuing, we were told that we were it, so with glass of refreshing hibiscus juice in hand we continued. Ngo explained that when he and Camille returned from living in Switzerland, they built the property from scratch …
Turns out that all the materials for the house that looked like it had been around for centuries had been lovingly up-cycled. So their future could be built from “fragments of the past”. We’re talking every brick (broken or whole), broken ceramic plates used in the mosaic structures - you get the picture. 
Camille is an artist and she designed the buildings and the garden that flank the Perfume River. Her artwork is on display throughout the property d you would be forgiven for thinking that the property was built to display her artwork but you’d be wrong. We entered the impressive and ornate music building where we were to be entertained. We knew that there was entertainment included but weren’t prepared for the recital was to come. Not only is Camille a skilled artist but she is an accomplished musician and singer and performing with her were three classical music professors from Hue University. They performed a repertoire of classical Vietnamese pieces played on traditional instruments. There were classical poems that Camille put to musical score and even some western pieces adapted for traditional instruments. Each piece was introduced by Ngo who the English translation for what we were about to hear. 
After the recital, we were taken to the dining room where a private dinner awaited us. The food was a selection of local dishes and it’s worth noting that having gone to the trouble of establishing dietaries the day before, the went shopping for fresh ingredients that morning.

So why do they do all this? Well it turns out that Camille just happens to be the sixth generation descendant of the last Emperor of Vietnam and the draw to return to Hue (historic capital of Vietnam) after 40 years in Europe prover too strong. They have done all this to preserve the traditional music and arts so they can share and continue to educate the culture they are so proud of. True benefactors of the arts!

They are two genuinely beautiful people that made us feel so welcome - Camille even applied cream to a mozzie bite on my face. This is not for everyone but it’s a cultural and hospitality experience we will never forget. Extraordinary experience that we would highly recommend to all who appreciate history and culture!

Estraordinary.
Jan 2026 • Family
A completely unique experience in Vietnam. This couple have made Hue their home once again after living in Europe for decades. They bring a reverence for Vietnamese music, art, design, and cuisine and have built the most extraordinary home and venue to showcase them. Mme Camille is a multi-faceted artist who has built it seemingly from the ground-up, yet it feels as if it has stood for centuries. It is impossible to describe the complete experience but in our case it began with a very personal concert by highly trained musical scholars, with vocal accompaniment by Madame. We then went into a beautiful, multi-course dinner. They make you feel as if you are their close personal friends. This is not an experience for everybody. It is elegant, refined, and utterly unique. It feels like a once-in-a-lifetime evening.

Ngo T
Dear Acmes,

Thank you very much for your generous and thoughtful review. We are deeply touched by your words.

You are right: we cherish the cultural heritage of all the countries in which we have lived, and especially that of our birthplace, Huế, Vietnam. With Bến Xuân Garden House Theatre, our wish has been to preserve, protect, continue, and further develop Vietnamese music, art, architecture, and cuisine. In designing and shaping this place, we have drawn inspiration from the heritage of our ancestors—in architecture, performance, painting, and culinary traditions—while allowing it to live and breathe in the present.

All of this we wish to share with our guests, because happiness grows when it is shared, and what we cherish together is more carefully protected for generations to come.

Thank you for allowing us to share this dinner recital with you, and for becoming part of the Bến Xuân story.

With our warmest regards,
Camille & Ngo

A Beautiful and Unforgettable Cultural Experience at a Hidden Gem in Hue
Mar 2025 • Family
We had the pleasure of discovering this hidden gem during our visit to Hue. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly welcomed by the owner of this beautiful riverside home. He gave us a private tour and shared the story behind the house. The atmosphere was serene, and we immediately felt calm and at peace.

We then met Mrs Camille, the incredibly talented co-owner who designed the house, created the beautiful paintings displayed inside, and later performed as the vocalist alongside three wonderful musicians during the musical experience. Before the performance, they kindly served us tea and sweets, which made us feel truly cared for.

The performance was intimate, emotional and interactive. We were invited to read the English translations of the lyrics before each song, which helped us connect even more with the music. Mrs Camille is so sweet and humble, and the couple are genuinely kind and passionate about what they do. Their love and respect for art, especially music and culture, really shine through as they welcome others with warmth, host charitable events and generously share their home, art and stories.

This experience was a highlight of our trip and something we will never forget. Highly recommended for anyone who appreciates art and meaningful cultural experiences.

Ngo T
Dear Baivari,
Thank you for your warm and detailed review. We appreciate very much that you value our effort in hosting our guests in this very personal way. I may write down what we have discussed and experienced.

"Cultural tourism at Bến Xuân Garden House Theatre is far more than a simple visit—it is an unforgettable experience.
Guests are invited to immerse themselves in the harmony of architecture, art, music, and cultural heritage. This shared journey fosters meaningful exchanges between host and guest, where both become participants in a deeper cultural dialogue.

All takes place in the intimate music chamber, crafted from ancient wood and echoing the refined warmth of noble houses from the Nguyễn dynasty. In this setting, the boundary between artist and audience dissolves. Emotions flow freely, touching hearts directly, and creating a true Zusammengehörigkeit—a sense of belonging—through shared experience.

Guests are encouraged to engage actively: before each piece, they may read translations of the lyrics in English, French, or German, depending on their language. This connection with the words deepens their resonance with the music, making each performance feel more personal, emotional, and interactive.

Here, guests are not merely listeners. They become part of the performance. This participatory spirit brings cultural values to life, forging deeper bonds and bringing people closer across cultures and time."

6 stars experience.
Feb 2024 • Friends
Food is always the top of our list of priorities when travelling and Vietnam is no different ,though some may think of Pho as the all consuming Vietnamese dish. 

I was looking for a fine dining restaurant to indulge and narrowed down to 2.
Ben Xuan Garden House was my choice after reading some positive reviews. 

I received an email reply from Ngo who said he would be happy to set a table for us.

It was all POSITIVE from the word GO ! Ngo called me and suggested the best approach to Ben Xuan was via a 25min boat ride down the perfume river. 

On arrival , Ngo warmly welcomed the 4 . We were served refreshments. He even helped snap a few Photos ( which he knew) would become a great conversation piece when friends ask about our visit to Hue. 

He then introduce his very charming wife Camille to us. We could sense that she was someone very special with multi - talented kills in painting , planning and restoring the Garden House to it's glory. 

After , a tour of the the compounds , Ngo ushered us into the main recital hall. As we did not see other guests, I thought we would be waiting a while for others to arrive. 
As it turns out it was going to be just the 4 of us ( overwhelming pleasant surprise ) . 

The "private" recital was like some surreal VIP entertainment . After 30 odd minutes or so, I was eager to savour the special cuisine prepared for us. 

Each of the dish served was exquisite and we couldn't help but snap enough fotos to fill a small album. 

A final comment is that Ben Xuan is not your typical fine dining restaurant but an all encompassing experience . 

We wish Camille and Ngo all the best of health as most Asians cherish a lot and success in their operation and passion in what they enjoy doing. 

I strongly recommend anyone who is thinking of visiting and meeting Camille and Ngo not to pass up the opportunity .

Best wishes to Camille and Ngo .

Lilian & Andy ( Singapore) Liz & Gabby ( Melbourne) .

An Enchanting Evening Not to Miss
Jan 2020 • Solo
A highlight of my SE Asia trip—and of my world travels—was the splendid evening spent at the gorgeous Ben Xuan Garden House Theatre in the company of its charming, sophisticated owners, Ngo and Camille. Vietnamese-born and European-educated, they recently returned to Hue as philanthropists after decades in Paris and Zurich. Camille, born into the royal family of the Nguyen dynasty, is lovely, a talented, versatile singer (Vietnamese folks songs to American jazz) who performed her East-West repertoire soulfully, accompanied by three university musicians on ancient instruments. After the beautiful private concert, I enjoyed a fine dinner and conversation with Ngo and Camille, whose mission of cultural exchange is inspired and inspiring. Simply unmissable!
